subject.title: Add confirmation step to /new and /reset to prevent accidental session wipes

question: Should OpenClaw require confirmation for explicitly typed destructive `/new` and hard `/reset` commands, and should that policy apply globally or only to selected UI surfaces?
rationale: Current main already protects the button-triggered New Session path, but typed commands remain immediate across multiple surfaces; changing that behavior or adding a config option is a UX/config contract decision.

options.title: Confirm typed destructive commands
options.body: Add one short-lived repeat-to-confirm or equivalent confirmation for typed `/new` and hard `/reset`, while preserving `/reset soft` and non-destructive commands.

options.title: Keep typed commands immediate
options.body: Treat explicitly typed `/new` and hard `/reset` as intentional expert commands and leave only click/tap affordances guarded.

options.title: Make confirmation configurable
options.body: Add an opt-out or step-count policy, accepting the extra config, docs, tests, and upgrade proof burden.

recommendation.title: Confirm typed destructive commands
recommendation.body: Add one short-lived repeat-to-confirm or equivalent confirmation for typed `/new` and hard `/reset`, while preserving `/reset soft` and non-destructive commands.

likelyOwner.reason: He recently merged the adjacent Control UI confirmation behavior and documented the typed-command scope boundary.
